div.head: ECf 11.1 B 4
div.ab: Filii enim regis gentes Christiane et populi regni sunt, qui sub uestra protectione et pace in regno degunt et consistunt, iuxta Euangelium: ‘Quemadmodum gallina congregat pullos sub alis’. Gentes uero regni Britannie et populi uestri sunt, quos diuisos debetis in unum ad concordiam et pacem et ad fidem et legem Christi et ad sanctam ecclesiam congregare, reuocare, fouere, manutenere, protegere, regere et ab iniuriosis et malitiosis et ab inimicis semper defendere.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 637 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 11, 1, and numbers 11, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 11, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

div.ab: For the Christian nations and peoples of the kingdom are the king's sons, who live and abide under your protection and peace in the kingdom, according to the Gospel: ‘As the hen gathers her chickens under her wings’. The nations of the kingdom of Britain and the peoples are yours, whom, being divided, you ought to gather into one, to concord and peace and to the faith and law of Christ and to holy Church, to recall, cherish, maintain, protect, rule, and always defend from wrongdoers and malicious men and from enemies.
